source_checks.requirement: Q3: What must a resident check before relying on a rebate?
source_checks.evidence: 01 / THE BRIEFING The detail behind the big promise. Useful local context starts with the responsible source. These are editorial snapshots, with checked dates and clear limits. 01 / REBATES A rebate headline is not an approval. Location, utility, program status, and purchase timing matter. Start with the right official route before putting an incentive in your budget. Read the rebate briefing ↗ 02 / THE FINE PRINT Old tax-credit copy can cost you. The IRS describes the Section 25C credit for improvements through 2025. Do not assume a new 2026 installation qualifies. Check the IRS timing rules ↗ 03 / HEAT PUMP PLANNING Look past the price tag. A useful comparison includes the scope, equipment, assessment, electrical work, and who handles program documentation. Start your question list ↗

source_checks.requirement: Q4: Does BEPS apply to every home?
source_checks.evidence: 02 / BEPS, WITHOUT THE GUESSWORK Start with your building. Building Energy Performance Standards are specific to covered buildings and jurisdictions. A condo resident’s questions can differ from a single-family homeowner’s. Read the resident BEPS guide ↗ MARYLAND / STATE PROGRAM 35,000 sq ft and above MDE identifies commercial and multifamily buildings at this size for its program, with exemption procedures. Confirm the actual building’s coverage. Check Maryland MDE ↗ MONTGOMERY COUNTY / LOCAL PROGRAM 25,000 sq ft and above The County describes coverage for most commercial and multifamily buildings at this size. Its rules need their own check. Read the County’s scope ↗ WASHINGTON, DC / OWN PROGRAM Use the District’s record. Start with DOEE’s current program and building-energy portal to check coverage and applicable requirements. Start with DC DOEE ↗ A performance gap alone does not establish noncompliance, required HVAC replacement, or a funded project. Confirm the building record and applicable requirements.

source_checks.requirement: Q5: Can a resource request be separate from newsletter signup?
source_checks.evidence: A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS Clear context. Clear expectations. Can you tell me which rebate I qualify for? + Our guides help you find the responsible program and prepare questions. The administrator determines eligibility. Program status, utility, income, equipment, contractor rules, and timing can change the answer. We do not promise approval or a rebate amount. Does BEPS mean every homeowner must replace their HVAC? + No. Start by checking whether a particular building is covered under the applicable jurisdiction’s program. A threshold or performance gap alone does not establish a replacement obligation. Condo boards and building managers should confirm the building’s record with the administrator. Is this a government or utility website? + MBRACE INSIGHT is an independent educational publication. We link to official agencies and programs so you can verify information directly. We do not claim government endorsement, privileged access, or authority to approve applications. Does a guide subscribe me to the newsletter? + Only if you select the separate, unchecked newsletter option. Resource requests and newsletter requests are recorded distinctly. Use the preference link shown after signup to withdraw your newsletter request. Will an email arrive immediately? + This private preview records requests and unlocks downloads after saving. Email confirmation and newsletter delivery are not connected yet. Newsletter requests remain pending confirmation; no email is sent automatically. How current is the briefing? + The source-checked date records our review, not an automatic live feed. Recheck official terms before a purchase or compliance decision. Send a correction or source to Max at mfisher@mbraceinsight.com .
